dive-dolphin.style: Photorealistic National Geographic / BBC Earth wildlife documentary still. Real wild dolphin with wet grey skin texture, subtle rake marks, water droplets, scientifically correct anatomy: rounded melon, rostrum, small dark eye, single crescent blowhole on top of the head, pectoral flippers, falcate dorsal fin, horizontal tail flukes (not a fish tail). Natural ocean or river lighting, god rays underwater. No cartoon, no 3D animation, no Pixar, no kawaii, no oversized human-like eyes, no anthropomorphic cartoon smile, no plastic toy look. No text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no logo. Child-appropriate educational science photo, no blood.

items.scene: A single wild common bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) swimming underwater, full body side view, scientifically accurate grey coloring darker on the back and paler below, wet skin, natural ocean blue background slightly out of focus. Iconic, clear dolphin portrait.
Wide open ocean: deep blue sea, waves, horizon, sunlight. A wild dolphin dorsal fin or a small pod in the open pelagic ocean. Emphasize OCEAN habitat, not a river.
A tropical freshwater RIVER with brown-green water, jungle banks, and a pink Amazon river dolphin (boto) surfacing. Clearly a river, not the sea.
Wild bottlenose dolphin diving steeply downward, head pointed to the depths, bubbles streaming up. Action of diving.
Bottlenose dolphin swimming horizontally with a strong tail-fluke stroke, streamlined, bubbles, clear water. The action of swimming.
Dolphins hunting: chasing and herding a school of silver fish underwater. Cooperative hunt, no blood. Focus on hunting behavior.
Wild dolphin playing with floating kelp, pushing or tossing seaweed. Natural play, not a beach ball, not children.
Bottlenose dolphin leaping high out of the ocean, full body in the air, splash below. The leap is the subject.

Close-up wildlife photo of a dolphin's PECTORAL FLIPPER (the side paddle-like limb), anatomically correct, grey wet skin, water. Not a scuba diving fin worn by a human unless very secondary. The animal flipper is the hero.
A dolphin DORSAL FIN cutting the ocean surface, falcate curved triangle, grey, with the back of a bottlenose just under the water. Real dolphin fin, not a horror-movie shark fin, not a fish.
Close-up of dolphin TAIL FLUKES: horizontal, two-lobed, notched in the middle, lifting from the water or powering a stroke. Mammal flukes, NOT a vertical fish tail.
From a small research boat, a person points toward wild dolphins in the distance on the ocean. Sense of 'there they are'. Photoreal, not a cartoon child.
A LARGE pod: many dolphins, a dozen or more, filling the frame underwater or at the surface. Emphasize quantity, many animals.
Tight close-up of a dolphin's BEAK/rostrum: jaws, teeth slightly visible, melon above, real skin texture. Dolphin beak, NOT a bird, NOT a duck.
Side portrait of a spinner dolphin with a noticeably LONG slender beak dominating the composition. The length of the beak is the point.
Side portrait of a bottlenose dolphin with a SHORT thick beak, clearly stubbier than a spinner. The shortness of the beak is the point.
Full-body bottlenose dolphin underwater clearly possessing flippers, a dorsal fin, and a tail, as if showing what dolphins have. Clean educational wildlife photo.
THESE striped dolphins in the foreground, a small group of Stenella coeruleoalba with real flank stripes, close to the camera. Demonstrative 'these ones'.

Close wildlife photo of a STRIPED DOLPHIN's flank: the authentic dark lateral stripe from the eye along the body. Real Stenella coeruleoalba field mark. NOT a zebra, NOT a tiger, NOT candy stripes, NOT vertical bars on a cartoon dolphin.
SOME dolphins (a few) in the open ocean in the foreground, with empty blue water beyond, suggesting a subset. Photoreal pod of three or four.
Dolphins living in their ocean home: swimming in a natural marine habitat with light from the surface. Habitat of living, not a house.
THIS one Atlantic spotted dolphin centered and closest to the camera, other water empty. Singular focus, 'this dolphin'.
Close-up of Atlantic spotted dolphin SKIN with real organic spots, mottled natural pattern. Dolphin spots, NOT a dalmatian dog, NOT a ladybug, NOT painted circles.
The OTHER kind: pink Amazon river dolphins in a river, contrasting with the idea of ocean dolphins. Freshwater boto habitat.
Three or four dolphins swimming tightly together, bodies almost touching, social togetherness.
Dolphins working: cooperatively circling a fish school, coordinated effort, serious hunting work, no blood.
A TEAM of dolphins in a coordinated hunting formation around fish, teamwork visible, several animals acting as one unit.
A dolphin WITH a piece of seaweed, holding or swimming with it. The 'with' relationship: dolphin and object together.
A dolphin investigating a natural THING in the water: a kelp blade, a drifting coconut, or a jellyfish-safe object. Curiosity toward an object.
THEY: two wild dolphins side by side looking toward the camera/slightly off, a pair as the pronoun they. Photoreal.
A dolphin fully immersed in clear WATER, caustics and light rays, the water itself beautiful and obvious. Underwater world.
Real ocean SEAWEED/kelp forest: long brown-green fronds waving, a dolphin weaving through kelp. Macroalgae, not cartoon grass.
A dolphin clearly enjoying play with kelp at the surface, energetic natural play that reads as 'like / enjoy'. No heart icons, no text.
Close-up of the single crescent BLOWHOLE on top of a dolphin's head, possibly exhaling spray. Accurate mammal blowhole, top of head, not a nose on the snout.
View of a dolphin's BACK from above or behind: smooth grey back with the dorsal fin rising from it. The back is the subject.
Dolphin oriented head-DOWN, descending into darker blue, bubbles going up. Direction: down.
Air and mist spraying THROUGH a dolphin's open blowhole at the surface. Motion of air passing through the hole.
Dolphin at the surface taking a breath of AIR, sky visible, spray, chest expanded. Air-breathing at the interface of water and sky.
Dolphin surfacing to BREATHE, blowhole open, inhale/exhale, droplets. The act of breathing.
A dolphin swimming urgently upward toward the bright surface because it needs to breathe, determined ascent from the depths.
Dolphins COMING up from below toward the shining water surface, approaching the top. Movement toward the viewer/surface.
Dolphin heads at the TOP of the water, the surface line, sky above, bodies below. The top/surface is clear.
A dolphin GETTING a breath of air, just after inhaling at the surface, water sheeting off the head. Obtaining air.
